question: Which accessible whole/part inspection or independent object measurement most efficiently restricts surviving positive quantity assignments?
outcome: In 24 new worlds per condition, information/rank identifies absolute quantities in 23 complete and 22 incomplete collections, versus random 15 and 17 and cost-first 0 and 1. Undercovered counts produce wrong unique answers in 21 information/rank worlds; withheld absolute measurements expose wrong scales that pass physical relations. A post-outcome overlap score, specified before 24 fresh valid-interval worlds, identifies six absolute vectors versus zero under each original policy and narrows scale intervals in 15 paired worlds. Exact positive alternatives certify all 28 retained relative ambiguities across the two endpoints.
challenge: Artificial relative normalization initially concealed the information from a scale measurement. The original interval score ignored the possible contraction from shifted intervals. Availability, incomplete contents and understated measurement errors create distinct failure cases.
remedy: Preserve pilot v1, separate acquired equalities from the gauge, reconstruct and verify exact LP certificates, keep hidden responses outside selection, compare original/refined rules on new worlds and retain all wrong, ambiguous and rejected assignments. Main and refinement reviews verify 4,794 states and 4,338 acquired actions; an all-available post-run diagnostic separates collection limits from budget failures.
retry_when: A new observation-selection rule, calibrated measurement distribution, measured collection access costs, observed contents-size bounds, uncertain label assignments or accession-linked physical pilot changes the test. Reuse existing frozen worlds for diagnostic comparisons and specify fresh seeds for a new policy endpoint.
